prior_narrative.tldr: AI labs and governments both formalized external oversight of frontier AI claims this month. OpenAI stood up an outside advisory group to vet its own mathematics results, and DeepSeek is now being pulled directly into intergovernmental AI-risk discussions.
prior_narrative.whats_new: DeepSeek is set to join a UN Security Council briefing on artificial intelligence risks, putting a Chinese frontier lab in a formal international risk-governance forum for the first time in this window.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Formal review is arriving from two directions at once — labs self-policing benchmark claims and governments pulling labs into oversight forums — so expect more requests to substantiate claims with independent evidence, not just vendor numbers.

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models", so most of it is a reading list, not one thread. Oct 9-27 items cover knowledge graphs, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, steering and continual learning.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 29: Mistral Large 4 is released, with vLLM day-0 support (sparse MLA, speculative decoding, NIXL prefill/decode on Blackwell) and a Hugging Face launch post.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Mistral Large 4 is the one item here you can deploy: serving support landed the same day as the weights, so self-hosting is testable now. The papers remain a reading list.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm Mistral Large 4's quality against DeepSeek and Cohere models?
Does the "9x price gap" comparison hold against first-party Mistral API pricing?
Does Reva's real-time screening keep false positives low enough to gate agent-written code?
Does CAMR's replay selection reduce forgetting on models larger than those in its experiments?
Does CANS steering preserve general capability on models beyond those it was tested on?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you self-host, pull Mistral Large 4 on the vLLM day-0 build and rerun your own evals and latency tests before swapping it in. Treat the Oct 22 price comparison as unverified until you check provider pricing pages.

prior_narrative.tldr: An Oct 22 paper (HERD) framed continual learning as a trade-off between parametric methods, which forget, and non-parametric ones. Three days later a benchmark began measuring whether LLM agents actually improve from experience over long horizons.
prior_narrative.whats_new: CAMR (Oct 27) proposes compatibility-aware memory replay, deciding whether incoming data is worth replaying before it is used to update an LLM.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agents that learn from experience need retention without regressions; replay selection and long-horizon evals are the pieces to watch before trusting self-improving setups.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers in six days; all research-stage, none shipped in a product.

prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: do not adopt, but add a retention check to any fine-tune or agent-memory pipeline that updates on new data.

storylines.label: Benchmarking Long-Horizon
storylines.latest_title: CALM: Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance for Long-Horizon Language Agents

prior_narrative.tldr: Doc2Harness opened the thread on Oct 14 by measuring how much the harness around a model, not just the model, drives long-horizon coding-agent results. Over the next week, papers added search-state learning (ClueFlow), error-recovery tests for computer-use agents (CUA-Recovery) and a continual-learning exam.
prior_narrative.whats_new: FOCUS (Oct 26) proposes active critic learning to fix credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards, moving the thread from measuring long-horizon agents to training them.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent failures come from harness design, silent state corruption and weak credit assignment, so benchmarks that isolate those factors are more useful for platform decisions than single-score leaderboards.

status.detail: Five arXiv preprints, no independent replication yet; benchmarks and training methods are arriving together.

beats.headline: Doc2Harness benchmarks harness engineering for coding agents
Search state and computer-use error recovery get their own tests
Continual learning and critic training extend the focus to improvement over time

open_questions: Does any of these benchmarks get adopted by a major lab or independent evaluator?
Do the reported FOCUS gains hold on a third-party long-horizon benchmark?
Will CUA-Recovery results show shipped computer-use agents detecting silent state corruption?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: When evaluating a long-horizon agent, rerun it under your own harness and add an injected-error recovery case before trusting a leaderboard score.
